question: A 38-year-old man presents to his primary care practitioner for 2 months of rectal bleeding. He also reports occasional diarrhea and abdominal pain. His family history is relevant for his father and uncle, who died from complications of colorectal cancer. Colonoscopy shows more than 10 colorectal adenomas. Which of the following genes is most likely affected in this patient?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Multiple colorectal adenomas" -> "Possible familial adenomatous polyposis (FAP)" -> "APC gene mutation" -> 95% CHAIN: "Rectal bleeding, diarrhea, abdominal pain" -> "Possible Lynch syndrome" -> "hMLH1 gene mutation" -> 80% CHAIN: "Family history of colorectal cancer" -> "Increased risk for hereditary cancer syndromes" -> "Possible TP53 gene mutation" -> 95%
analysis: Given the patient's presentation of multiple colorectal adenomas and a family history of colorectal cancer, the most likely gene affected in this patient is APC (adenomatous polyposis coli) gene. Mutations in the APC gene are associated with familial adenomatous polyposis (FAP), which predisposes individuals to develop numerous colorectal adenomas and increases the risk of colorectal cancer.
